admin.logging.intro: The logging is the history of backups, restores, downloads, prunes and deletions, with the output of borg. Set per type how long it is kept, or delete old logging by hand. A task that is still running is never deleted. The backups themselves are always kept.
admin.logging.keep_hint: 0 means: keep forever. Older logging is deleted right after saving, and automatically every hour after that.

restore.confirm_overwrite: Existing files at the destination will be overwritten. Continue?
restore.destination_hint: Absolute path on the target, for example /restore. With / the files return to their original place. For Local this is a path in the Locutus container; the data directory and system directories of Locutus are protected.

restore.intro: First choose the client to restore to and then the directory the files go into. The files keep their path from the backup below that directory: with destination /restore, /etc/hosts ends up in /restore/etc/hosts.
restore.overwrite_hint: Off: files that already exist at the destination are skipped. On: they are replaced by the version from the backup.
restore.title: Restore
role.admin.description: Manages identity providers (OIDC/SAMLv2), users, roles, systems and the logging. Has no access to backups, files or restores.
role.backupper.description: Everything a restorer can do, and also manages the backup and prune schedules of assigned clients.
role.restorer.description: Everything a viewer can do, and can also download files and directories from archives of assigned systems or restore them to assigned clients or into Locutus.
role.viewer.description: Sees the backups, restores and the contents of the archives of assigned systems, but cannot change or download anything.
schedule.cron_syntax: Per field: * (every), a number, a list (1,15), a range (1-5) or a step (*/15, 8-18/2). When both the day of the month and the weekday are restricted, it runs when either one matches.
schedule.desc.hourly: Every hour at %d minutes past the hour
schedule.desc.hours: Every %d hours, at %d minutes past the hour (from 00:%02d)
schedule.example.office: on weekdays every hour from 08:15 up to and including 18:15
schedule.example.quarterly: on the 1st of Jan, Apr, Jul and Oct at 02:00
schedule.invalid: This schedule is invalid or never runs.
schedule.kind.hourly: Every hour or every few hours

system.prune_public_key_hint: Put this key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the repository server, restricted to 'borg serve' without --append-only and preferably only from the IP address of Locutus (see the README).
system.prune_ssh_key_help: Only needed when the normal SSH key is restricted to 'borg serve --append-only' on the repository server. Locutus then uses this key itself for prune and compact only; it is never forwarded to clients.
system.prune_ssh_key_hint: (optional; private key, without a password; or generate one)
system.prune_ssh_key_remove: Remove prune key (prune and compact then use the normal SSH key)
system.public_key_client_hint: Put this key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the SSH user on the client, with agent forwarding allowed and optionally the Locutus wrapper as command (see the README).
system.public_key_repo_hint: Put this key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the SSH user on the repository server, restricted to 'borg serve' (see the README).
system.repo_path_hint_local: Absolute path in the container; mount the directory as a volume in docker-compose.yml.

system.use_sudo: Run borg and restores with sudo
system.use_sudo_hint: Locutus logs in as the SSH user above and starts borg (and, for a restore, stat and tar) with 'sudo -n'. This way all files can be backed up and restored without logging in as root. You set up sudo on the client yourself (see the README).
